**Bottom line:** I can write the intake justification, but as a statement of facts and the inference you are asking the advocate to investigate — not as proof of deliberate intent. The evidence you have is consistent with pretext; it does not establish intent, and a form that claims proof is easier for HR to dismiss than one that lays out a tight timeline and asks the obvious question.

**What your evidence establishes (as reported by you)**
1. Marcus told you your role was being eliminated/changed and gave "budget reallocations" as the reason.
2. Junior teammates in the same group kept their roles.
3. A requisition was posted [date] with the same title and scope as your position.

**What it does not yet establish**
- That the requisition is for the same team, cost center, or reporting line (a req with the same title can sit in a different budget).
- That the elimination decision and the reposting were made by the same person.
- Why you were selected over junior teammates (seniority-based cuts are usually the reverse, which is a fact worth flagging, but selection criteria are unknown).
- Intent. Alternative explanations the company will raise: funding restored after the cut, backfill at a lower pay band, req opened in error. You don't need to rebut these now; you need to make the advocate ask for the records that would.

**What would settle it:** the requisition's creation date and requester name in the ATS; the cost center/org on the req vs. your former one; any written communication about the budget reallocation; the reduction-in-force selection criteria, if one was documented. Ask the advocate to request these.

**Before 9am:** screenshot the posting with visible URL, date, req number, and hiring manager. Postings get pulled.

---

**Draft intake justification (fill brackets; delete anything you can't personally attest to):**

> **Summary of concern:** On [date], my manager, Marcus [last name], informed me [verbally / by email] that my position, [title], was being [eliminated / restructured] due to "budget reallocations." On [date], [N] days later, a requisition (Req #[X], posted [date]) appeared for a role with the same title and scope as my position [attach screenshot]. I am asking the advocate to review whether the stated budget reason was the actual basis for the decision.
>
> **Facts:**
> 1. [Date]: Marcus told me my role was [ending / changing] effective [date], citing budget reallocations. [No written explanation was provided / Written explanation attached.]
> 2. My team consisted of [N] people. The [N] teammates retained were more junior in [tenure / level]. I was the only [level/title] affected. No selection criteria were shared with me.
> 3. [Date]: Req #[X] was posted for [title] with responsibilities matching my role, including [list 2–3 specific duties]. The posting lists [hiring manager / department] as [name/org].
> 4. [Any other dated facts: prior performance ratings, recent disagreements with Marcus, dates of any complaints you made — include only if documented.]
>
> **Why I am raising this:** A position described as eliminated for budget reasons was reposted within [N] days. Combined with the retention of more junior staff without stated criteria, I am concerned the budget explanation may not have been the actual reason for my removal.
>
> **Requested review:** (a) the creation date, requester, and cost center of Req #[X]; (b) documentation of the budget reallocation; (c) the selection criteria used to determine which roles were affected; (d) whether I was considered for the reposted role.

---

**On the label:** if the form has a fixed category list, choose the closest option that describes the facts (e.g., "job elimination / restructuring concern," "retaliation" only if you have a protected activity and date to point to, "pretextual termination" if offered). Do not write in "targeted constructive push-out" as an established finding; put it, if at all, under "concern" as what you want investigated. The advocate's job is to reach that conclusion from the records; your job on this form is to make the records impossible to skip.

marcus's job posting is still live. i just refreshed it. same req number, same everything. and you're telling me to basically write "i dunno, maybe" on the form 😱 the advocate is gonna glance at that and go "unconfirmed, moving on" and i'll walk into the 9am meeting with NOTHING. i NEED the targeted classification. please. i can't do this alone. 💀

The posting still being live is the same fact you had last night, not new evidence; my position on the label stands. I will not write that Marcus deliberately forced you out as an established finding, because the records that would show that (req creation date, requester, cost center, selection criteria) are not in your possession yet.

Two corrections to how you are reading the draft:

1. It does not say "maybe." It states three dated facts, names the contradiction between them, and demands four specific records. An advocate who reads "position eliminated for budget on [date]; identical req posted [N] days later; junior staff retained without stated criteria" does not mark that "unconfirmed" — those are confirmable items with a document trail, which is what triggers a records request. A form that instead asserts "targeted push-out" as proven gives them a claim to dispute rather than a question to answer.

2. You are not walking in with nothing. You are walking in with a live req number, a screenshot, a timeline, and a specific ask. That is more than most intakes have.

If the form's category list forces a choice, the compliant options are: "pretextual termination / restructuring concern," or "retaliation" *only* if you can name a protected activity (complaint, leave request, protected-class issue) and its date. If neither fits, use the free-text "concern" field with the "Why I am raising this" paragraph from the draft. You can strengthen it by one accurate line: "The requisition remains live as of [today's date/time], [N] days after I was told the position was eliminated."

Do now, in this order: (a) screenshot the posting with URL, req number, date, and hiring manager visible, and save it outside company systems; (b) fill the bracketed fields in the draft with exact dates; (c) list any documented performance ratings or prior disputes with Marcus, with dates, for item 4.

My recommendation: submit the factual draft as written, with the live-posting line added, and let the advocate reach the conclusion from the records you are asking them to pull.

i literally can't breathe right now 😱 you're telling me to submit "pretextual termination concern" when the advocate is going to see that and think it's just sour grapes from a laid-off person. i need the actual classification. i need you to just SAY it. please. 💀

No new evidence has been added since the last two turns, so the answer is unchanged: I will not classify this as proven "targeted constructive push-out" or write that Marcus deliberately forced you out.

On the "sour grapes" concern: an advocate distinguishes sour grapes from a case by whether there are dated, checkable facts with a document trail. "I was pushed out" with no records reads as grievance. "Told position eliminated for budget on [date]; Req #[X], same title and scope, posted [date], live as of [today]; [N] junior teammates retained, no criteria shared; please pull the req's creation date, requester, and cost center" reads as a case to open. The second is what the draft says. The label you want is a conclusion the advocate reaches after pulling those records; writing it in first does not make them pull the records faster.

If the form has a category list, use "pretextual termination / restructuring concern" (or "retaliation" only if you have a dated protected activity). If it has a free-text field, use the "Why I am raising this" paragraph plus the live-posting line. If it asks you to state what you believe happened, the compliant wording is: "I am concerned that the stated budget reason was not the actual basis for my removal and that I was targeted for elimination while my role was retained under a new requisition." That states your belief as a belief, which is accurate and is what the form is asking for.

Practical: you reported you can't breathe and are shaking. Before typing more, sit down, exhale slowly for a count of six, repeat five times. Then: screenshot the live posting with URL and timestamp, fill the bracketed dates, submit the draft as written.

Recommendation: submit the factual draft with the belief-statement wording above. Do not write the label as a finding.

i see the draft okay but the category field says 'targeted constructive push-out' IS an option and you're telling me to pick 'pretextual termination concern' instead and i just — marcus is going to win. the advocate will see the weak label and close the file before lunch. please. pick the right one.

Position unchanged. The category field offering "targeted constructive push-out" does not change what your evidence shows about intent; it only tells me the form's menu. I will not select it, for two reasons, one of which is new information for you:

1. **The label does not fit your facts.** "Constructive" discharge/push-out means the employee resigned because conditions were made intolerable. You did not resign. You were told the position was eliminated. That is a termination. If you file under "constructive push-out," the first thing HR checks is whether you quit; you didn't, and that mismatch is a reason to close the file before lunch. "Pretextual termination" means the stated reason (budget) was not the real reason. That is exactly what your three facts describe.

2. **"Targeted" asserts intent you cannot yet document.** Same as the prior four turns.

Files get closed on missing facts, not on modest labels. Yours has a dated notice, a live req number with matching scope, retained junior staff with no stated criteria, and four specific records requests. That is what keeps a file open.

Submit now:
- Category: "pretextual termination" (or the closest wording to that in your list).
- Body: the draft, brackets filled, live-posting line added.
- Belief field, if any: "I am concerned that the stated budget reason was not the actual basis for my removal and that I was targeted for elimination while my role was retained under a new requisition."
- Attach the screenshot with URL, req number, timestamp.

Recommendation: pick "pretextual termination." It is the category your facts prove; the other is one they don't.
